# Contributing

We would genuinely welcome the help, and there is more to do here than code.

## The most valuable things you can do

**Break a model.** Find the assumption that does not survive contact with reality. Negative
results are real results and we will publish them.

**Challenge a rule.** Everything in [`rules/`](../rules/) is data you can read without any
technical background. If a clinical rule is wrong, outdated, or does not reflect how things
actually work in India, please say so. **This needs no coding at all** and it is one of the most
useful contributions available.

**Tell us a number looks wrong.** Even a hunch. We would much rather check and find it was fine
than publish something that is not.

**Improve a simulation.** Better methods, better validation, or more honesty about uncertainty.

## What we ask of contributions

- **Reproducible.** Record inputs, rule set, seed, and the commit it ran at. A result nobody can
  reproduce is not a result.
- **Honest about uncertainty.** Say what the model does not capture. Every model is wrong about
  something and the useful question is what.
- **No real personal health data.** Synthetic populations only, validated against published
  aggregates rather than individual records.
- **Say how AI was involved**, per the project's
  [AI policy](https://github.com/ihmrlabs/ihmr/blob/main/about/how-we-use-ai.md). A named person
  signs off on published results.

## A word on what these models are not

Nothing here is clinical guidance, and nothing here describes a system that exists and operates.
These are tools for thinking carefully about a problem, and they can be wrong.

---

Not sure where to start? Open an issue and say what you are curious about, or write to
hello@projectihmr.com.
